# Can One Solely Attribute the Solution Discrepancy Between OSQP and CVXOPT to Solver Implementation Errors?

> **Current answer:** Cannot. The maintainer tested `cond(P) ≈ 9.86 × 10^6` on the author's data and noted that the heuristic scaling of OSQP may not fully resolve ill-conditioned problems. The default tolerance of first-order methods is more lenient than that of the reference solver. The experiments in threads were tightened to `eps_abs/eps_rel = 1e-9`, and `max_iter` was increased as needed. Since the author did not report the final result, this is a data-supported diagnostic, not a general parameter answer.
